- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from 3rd–5th day onward with sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67); use 20-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often ignores downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or neutral; otherwise, allow for momentum continuation.
- For sentiment history with high variance (e.g., 0.00–1.00 alternating), apply smoothing filter: average of last 3 sentiment values to weight forecast adjustment.
